q: A close-ended scheme:
o: Has a fixed maturity and is listed on an exchange post-NFO
e: Close-ended schemes have fixed maturity. After NFO, units are NOT redeemable directly — they must be traded on an exchange where listed.

q: The lock-in period for an ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) is:
e: ELSS has a 3-year lock-in — the SHORTEST among all 80C investments. Tax deduction up to ₹1.5 lakh under Section 80C (old regime).

q: Maximum NFO period (other than ELSS) is:
e: NFO of an open-ended scheme cannot exceed 15 days. ELSS can have a 30-day NFO.

q: An Index Fund aims to:
o: Replicate the performance of an index
e: Index funds passively track and replicate index performance. Tracking error is the deviation from benchmark — lower is better.

q: An Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) is:
o: Bought and sold only via the AMC
Listed and traded on stock exchanges like a share
e: ETFs trade on exchanges in real-time. Authorized Participants create/redeem in creation units directly with the AMC.

q: A Fund of Funds (FoF) invests in:
e: FoF invests in units of other mutual fund schemes. Note: TER includes both FoF expenses and underlying scheme expenses (cap of 2.25%).

q: A Liquid Fund invests primarily in:
o: Debt instruments with maturity up to 91 days
e: Liquid funds invest in money market and debt instruments with residual maturity up to 91 days. Used as a parking option vs savings account.

q: A Balanced Advantage / Dynamic Asset Allocation Fund is classified as:
e: Hybrid scheme. Dynamically manages equity-debt allocation based on market valuations to reduce volatility.

q: For a scheme to qualify as an EQUITY-oriented scheme for taxation, minimum equity allocation must be:
e: For taxation, an equity-oriented fund must invest 65% or more in domestic equities. Below this, debt taxation rules apply.

q: Solution-oriented schemes (Retirement Fund, Children's Fund) typically have a lock-in of:
o: 5 years or until retirement/majority — whichever is earlier
e: Solution-oriented schemes have a 5-year lock-in OR until retirement/majority, whichever is earlier.

q: A Gilt Fund invests primarily in:
e: Gilt funds invest exclusively in Government Securities (Central + State). Zero credit risk but high interest-rate risk.

q: A scheme that allows entry/exit only at specified intervals is:
e: Interval schemes are open for subscription/redemption only at predetermined intervals (specified transaction periods).

q: ELSS lock-in period is:
e: 3 years — shortest among 80C options.

q: Maximum NFO period for non-ELSS open-ended scheme:
e: 15 days.

q: Equity-oriented scheme requires minimum equity allocation of:
e: 65%+ for equity tax treatment.

q: Liquid funds invest in instruments with maturity up to:
e: 91 days residual maturity.

q: Index funds aim to:
e: Passively replicate index performance.

q: A focused equity scheme can hold a maximum of how many stocks?
e: SEBI scheme categorisation: Focused funds invest in a maximum of 30 stocks, with concentration on a smaller universe of high-conviction picks.

q: Multi-cap funds, as per SEBI categorisation, must invest a minimum of __% each in large-cap, mid-cap, and small-cap stocks.
e: Multi-cap funds must invest a minimum of 25% each in large-cap, mid-cap, and small-cap stocks (total at least 75% in equity).

q: An Arbitrage Fund typically invests in:
o: Cash market and futures market simultaneously to capture spreads
e: Arbitrage funds simultaneously buy in cash market and sell in futures (or vice versa) to capture price spreads. Treated as equity for tax (≥65% equity exposure).

q: A scheme with mandate-allocated equity exposure between 65% and 80% (with debt 20-35%) is best categorized as:
e: Aggressive Hybrid: 65-80% equity, 20-35% debt. Balanced Hybrid: 40-60% equity. Conservative Hybrid: 10-25% equity.

q: Smart Beta funds aim to:
o: Capture systematic factor premia (value, momentum, quality, low-vol) using rules-based portfolios
Beat the market through active stock picking
e: Smart Beta funds use rules-based, factor-tilted strategies (value, momentum, quality, low volatility) — between passive and active.

q: Index Funds are subject to:
o: Some tracking error due to expenses, cash holdings and rebalancing lags
Higher tracking error than active funds
Tracking error only on rebalancing days
e: All index funds have some tracking error due to expenses, cash drag and rebalancing imperfections — though aim to minimize it.

q: In the sectoral and thematic funds category, an AMC can launch:
o: Only one such scheme per AMC
As many schemes as they want, subject to the condition that overlap between two funds is less than 50%
Up to a maximum of 5 such funds
e: AMCs can launch multiple sectoral/thematic schemes provided portfolio overlap between any two such schemes is less than 50%.

q: A focused equity fund holds 28 stocks. Maximum permitted under SEBI:
e: SEBI scheme categorisation caps Focused funds at 30 stocks.

q: A close-ended scheme has 10 cr units outstanding, total NAV ₹15 per unit, but trades on the exchange at ₹13. The discount to NAV is:
e: Discount = (15 - 13) / 15 = 13.33%. Close-ended scheme units often trade at discount/premium to NAV in the secondary market.

q: A Value fund (per SEBI scheme categorisation) must invest a minimum of __ in equity and equity-related instruments:
e: Value funds (and Contra funds) must invest at least 65% in equity and equity-related instruments. Mutual fund AMC can offer either Value or Contra — not both.

q: An AMC offering a Value fund:
o: Can also offer a Contra fund
Cannot also offer a Contra fund
Must also offer a Growth fund
e: Per SEBI categorisation, an AMC can offer EITHER a Value fund OR a Contra fund — not both. They're considered substitutes.

q: Dividend yield fund must invest a minimum of __ in dividend-yielding stocks:
e: Dividend Yield funds must invest at least 65% in dividend-yielding stocks (per SEBI categorisation).

q: A Liquid Fund invests in instruments with Macaulay duration up to:
e: Liquid funds: portfolio Macaulay duration up to 91 days. Instruments are typically money-market and short-term debt.

q: An "Ultra Short Duration Fund" has portfolio Macaulay duration of:
e: Ultra Short Duration Fund: Macaulay duration 3-6 months. Sits between Liquid and Low Duration in the SEBI debt categorisation.

q: A "Low Duration Fund" has portfolio Macaulay duration of:
e: Low Duration Fund: Macaulay duration 6-12 months. Higher than Ultra Short, lower than Short Duration.

q: A "Short Duration Fund" has portfolio Macaulay duration of:
e: Short Duration Fund: portfolio Macaulay duration of 1-3 years per SEBI categorisation.

q: A "Conservative Hybrid Fund" must invest __ in equity:
e: Conservative Hybrid: 10-25% equity, 75-90% debt. Lowest equity exposure among hybrid categories.

q: A "Balanced Hybrid Fund" must invest __ in equity:
e: Balanced Hybrid: 40-60% equity, 40-60% debt. Roughly balanced allocation.

q: An "Aggressive Hybrid Fund" must invest __ in equity:
e: Aggressive Hybrid: 65-80% equity, 20-35% debt. Equity-tilted hybrid; taxed as equity-oriented.

q: A Multi Asset Allocation Fund must invest minimum __ in each of at least __ asset classes:
e: Multi Asset: minimum 10% in EACH of at least 3 asset classes (e.g., equity, debt, gold/REITs).

q: An Equity Savings Fund typically:
o: Holds equity (≥65% gross via cash + arbitrage), debt, and uses arbitrage to reduce net equity
e: Equity Savings: ≥65% in equity (gross — including arbitrage hedges), some debt. Net unhedged equity is lower than gross. Taxed as equity-oriented.

q: An AMC offering a Multi-cap fund:
o: Cannot also offer a Flexi-cap fund
Can also offer a Flexi-cap fund (separate categorisation)
Must also offer a Sector fund
e: Multi-cap (25% each in large/mid/small) and Flexi-cap (no cap restrictions, fund manager flexibility) are separate SEBI categories. AMC can offer both.

q: A Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) is:
o: A higher-risk category between mutual funds and PMS, with Risk-Band (5 levels) instead of Riskometer
e: SIFs are a SEBI-introduced category sitting between MFs and PMS — designed for sophisticated strategies. Use a Risk-Band (5 levels) given higher risk, not the Riskometer.

q: A Fund of Funds (FoF) investing in equity-oriented MF schemes is currently taxed:
o: As debt fund (slab rate) for all FoFs
As equity-oriented if it invests ≥90% in domestic equity-oriented schemes (post Budget 2024)
e: Post Budget 2024, FoFs investing ≥90% in domestic equity-oriented MF schemes can qualify for equity taxation (12.5% LTCG above ₹1.25L). Other FoFs taxed as debt.

q: A close-ended scheme typically:
o: Has a fixed maturity, NFO units listed on stock exchange for trading; AMC does not repurchase
e: Close-ended schemes have fixed maturity. After NFO closure, units are listed on the exchange — investors must transact via the exchange (often at discount/premium to NAV).

q: For a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) — it is regulated by:
e: REITs (and InvITs) are regulated by SEBI. Mutual fund schemes can hold REIT units, with prescribed allocation limits.

q: For an Equity Savings Fund — equity exposure (≥65%) is calculated INCLUDING:
o: Direct equity + arbitrage hedged equity (gross equity)
e: Equity Savings: gross equity (direct + arbitrage) ≥65% qualifies it as equity-oriented for tax. Net unhedged equity is much lower — providing a smoother return profile.

q: A scheme with 80% equity and 20% debt is best categorised as:
e: Aggressive Hybrid: 65-80% equity, 20-35% debt. Taxed as equity-oriented (≥65% equity).

q: Macaulay duration of an Ultra Short Duration Fund is:
e: Ultra Short Duration: 3-6 months Macaulay duration per SEBI categorisation.

q: A "Sector Fund" investing in a single sector is:
o: Less risky than a diversified fund
Riskier than a diversified fund (concentration risk)
e: Sector funds carry concentration risk — narrow exposure means sector-specific downturns hit hard. Higher risk than diversified equity funds.
